title: Sinonasal, pharynx and neck spaces

steps.tx: Vascular sinonasal masses present with distinctive clinical demographics and remodelling signs. **Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma** characteristically arises near the sphenopalatine foramen in adolescent males, causing anterior bowing of the posterior wall of the maxillary antrum, known as the **Holman-Miller sign**, on axial CT and MR imaging.

steps.tx: Sinonasal infections in severely compromised patients can rapidly become life-threatening. Invasive fungal **rhinosinusitis** caused by Mucorales or Aspergillus presents in immunocompromised hosts with bone destruction, intrasinus soft tissue, and hypoenhancement indicating devascularized tissue, recognized as the **black turbinate sign** on contrast-enhanced MR studies.

steps.tx: Epithelial neoplasms of the Schneiderian membrane show distinctive convolution patterns. **Inverted papilloma** originates on the lateral nasal wall near the middle turbinate, demonstrating a **cerebriform** convoluted columnar pattern on T2 and contrast-enhanced T1 MRI, with 10% harbouring synchronous or metachronous squamous cell carcinoma.

steps.tx: Deep cervical spaces require systematic cross-sectional analysis using vector displacement. **Parapharyngeal space** tumours are localized by displacement patterns: deep **parotid** lobe lesions displace parapharyngeal fat anteromedially, whereas carotid space schwannomas displace fat anteriorly, and masticator space lesions displace it posteromedially.

steps.tx: Oropharyngeal sepsis can precipitate septic vascular complications in young individuals. **Lemierre syndrome** is septic thrombophlebitis of the **internal jugular vein** caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum, classically arising from an oropharyngeal or peritonsillar abscess with septic pulmonary emboli presenting as cavitating peripheral lung nodules.

steps.tx: Accurate cross-sectional staging determines surgical resectability of mucosal malignancies in the head and neck. **Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma** invading through **thyroid cartilage** or cricoid cartilage into extralaryngeal soft tissues upstages the tumour to T4a, precluding organ-preservation radiotherapy and requiring total laryngectomy with postoperative chemoradiation.

steps.tx: Congenital lateral cervical anomalies demonstrate predictable spatial relationships. **Branchial cleft cyst** second type is the most common lateral neck cystic mass (95%), located anteromedial to the **sternocleidomastoid** muscle at the angle of the mandible, lateral to the carotid bifurcation and posterior to the submandibular gland.

right.title: Thyroglossal Duct Cyst
points: Most common midline paediatric neck cyst
Located along course of thyroglossal tract
Embedded in or adjacent to hyoid bone

steps.tx: Midline congenital cervical anomalies arise along embryonic thyroid migratory corridors. **Thyroglossal duct cyst** represents a midline or paramedian unilocular cyst along the tract of thyroid descent between the **foramen cecum** and the base of the neck, moving upwards on tongue protrusion due to intimate hyoid bone attachments.
